title: Permission Audit Schema and Rollout Checklist
body:
Permission Audit Schema and Rollout Checklist — RBAC v2 companion

TL;DR
We need a single, backward-compatible audit event contract that supports: attribute-anchored RBAC (user attributes + resource attributes), SIEM-friendly exports, automated evidence bundles for entitlement changes, and a phased migration checklist to reduce blast radius. This doc captures the proposed schema, validation checklist, migration heatmap, and an operational rollout plan for the next 8 weeks.

Background and motivation
- RBAC v2 introduces attribute-anchored permissions and decouples role-assignment from effective entitlements. That increases expressivity but complicates auditing and SIEM consumption.
- Current RBAC v1 audit logs are action-focused and sparse on attribute context (e.g., missing resource tags, cached attribute snapshot). We must produce a richer, deterministic export so security teams and SIEM can reconstruct who had what access when.

Goals
1) Design an audit event contract (JSON) usable by internal consumers and external SIEMs.
2) Create automated evidence packages that tie entitlement changes to source artifacts (PRs, policy edits, canary rollouts).
3) Provide a pragmatic migration checklist with verification and rollback triggers.

Scope
- In scope: permission grants/denials, role/attribute changes, policy edits, entitlements evaluation snapshots, proof-of-change artifacts, SIEM export transformations.
- Out of scope: telemetry for model inference usage (separate pipeline), detailed SSO assertion contents (we will reference assertion IDs).

Audit event contract (proposal)
- Event envelope (top-level fields): event_id, timestamp_utc, event_type, source_service, request_id, correlation_id, severity
- Principal (actor): principal_id, principal_type (user/service/robot), identity_provider, auth_strength, principal_attributes (list of key=value)
- Action: action_name (string), action_category (read/write/admin), api_route, resource_type, resource_id (canonical), resource_attributes (list of key=value), resource_owner_id
- Entitlement snapshot: evaluation_version, effective_permissions (list of permission strings), decision (allow/deny/conditional), policy_ids (list), evaluation_context_hash
- Evidence: evidence_type (policy-edit, role-bind, attribute-sync, manual-approval), evidence_id (UUID), actor_change_request (optional URL/PR id), before_digest, after_digest, signed_by (service id), evidence_retention_ttl_days
- Compliance hints: pii_present (true/false), pii_masking_strategy, exportable_to_siem (true/false)

Notes on canonical names and datatypes
- Use snake_case for all keys. Strings only for IDs and types. Lists of short strings for arrays. Keep permission names stable and versioned (e.g., perms:v2/compute.instance.start).
- evaluation_context_hash is a deterministic SHA256 over (principal_attributes + resource_attributes + policy_ids + model_version) so that subsequent audits can prove same inputs.

SIEM export shape (flattened JSON for ingestion)
- Many SIEMs prefer flattened fields. Provide two export modes: raw_event (full nested payload) and flat_event (all fields moved to top-level with dot-notation).
- Example flat keys: event_id, ts, src, principal.id, principal.type, action.name, resource.type, resource.id, decision, effective_perms_count, evidence.id
- Include a small transform library (Python) that converts raw_event -> flat_event and maps to common SIEM schemas (Elastic ECS, Splunk CIM). See linked_artifacts PR for initial transform.

Evidence automation: what an evidence package contains
- Required: evidence_id, evidence_type, timestamp, authoring_user_id, change_diff (text summary), signed_manifest (service signature), source_refs (PR link, Confluence doc id), evaluation_context_hash
- Optional: snapshot_payload_url (s3/gcs signed URL), screenshots or CSV attachments (zipped, with checksum)
- Evidence TTL and retention: default 365 days; high-risk policy changes keep 7 years per compliance requests (flagged by tags).

Migration heatmap and risk matrix (working notes)
- Highest risk: resource-owner role changes that cascade across cross-account resources. Require manual approval and two-step migration.
- Medium risk: attribute sync changes (e.g., dept -> team mapping). Mitigate with shadow-evals and weekly diff reports.
- Low risk: feature-flag toggles for limited-scope system roles. Canary release to 5% of traffic.

Validation checklist (automated + manual steps)
Automated verification (pre-rollout):
- [ ] Unit tests for event contract serialization/deserialization (SEC-412)
- [ ] Schema conformance tests against sample events (Elastic ECS mapping)
- [ ] Shadow SIEM exports for 72 hours to compare flat vs existing logs (metric: event field coverage >= 95%)
- [ ] Hash-stability check: identical eval context -> same evaluation_context_hash across repeated runs

Manual checks (pre-rollout gate):
- [ ] Access review: run targeted simulated access checks for top 50 risky resources
- [ ] Evidence completeness spot-check (pick 10 random policy edits; verify evidence package contains source_refs and signed_manifest)

Rollout plan (phases)
Phase 0 — Canary + dev-only (1 week)
- Deploy audit contract changes to dev and staging only.
- Enable raw_event writes and shadow flat_event exports.
- Verify transform library mapping to SIEM test index.
- Accept criteria: no more than 5% malformed events, no PII leakage beyond flagged fields.

Phase 1 — Internal tenant canary (2 weeks)
- Release to internal accounts and a small set of customers (opt-in).
- Enable evidence automation on policy-change endpoints.
- Monitoring: track evaluation latency increase; must be < 5ms p50 added overhead.
- Rollback trigger: >0.5% increase in entitlement evaluation errors or any evidence signing failures.

Phase 2 — Org-wide (3 weeks)
- Flip defaults for new policy edits to produce RBAC v2 evidence.
- Run nightly reconciliation jobs comparing v1 event replay to v2 flattened exports to detect divergence.
- Run access-review automation for high-risk resources.

Phase 3 — Cutover and cleanup (1 week)
- Migrate downstream SIEM mappings to consume flat_event as primary (maintenance window).
- Archive v1 audit indices after 30 days of parallel run, keep cold storage per retention policy.

Rollback and remediation playbook (short)
- If severe errors: disable evidence signing service, revert to raw_event only, and suspend flat exports.
- For noisy divergence: enable shadow mode and auto-reopen the last good policy bundle via the versioned policy store.
- Postmortem: create SEC postmortem ticket (SEC-458) with timeline and remediation steps.

Verification test plan (examples)
- Test case 1: role-bind change (manual PR) -> expect evidence package with PR link, before_digest, after_digest and signed_manifest.
- Test case 2: attribute sync (HR -> IAM) mismatch -> expect denial events with evaluation_context_hash differing; create alert to #sec-rbac and create ticket.
- Test case 3: API route that escalates permission -> verify flat_event contains action_category=admin and effective_perms_count incremented.

Monitoring and dashboards (owners)
- Dashboard 1 (SRE): audit event rate, malformed events, evidence signing latency (owner: platform-eng).
- Dashboard 2 (SecOps): policy-change volume, high-risk resource edits, evidence completeness ratio (owner: security ops).
- Alerts: evidence_signature_failures > 5/min; evaluation_errors_rate > 0.5% over 15m.

Open questions / decisions needed
- Long-term: store full snapshot payloads in cold storage (cost) vs store only signed manifests + digests. Trade-offs? (Owners: Platform + Finance)
- How to surface conditional permissions in flat_event without exploding cardinality? Suggested: include decision_condition_id and link to compact condition catalog.
- PII handling: do we redact principal attributes by default or provide a flag per index?

Next steps and action items
- Elena: finalize schema and push to Confluence by 2024-03-11.
- Marcus: wire up shadow SIEM export and provide test index by 2024-03-08.
- Priya: prepare evidence-signing library integration tests and PR (github PR referenced above).
- Schedule cross-team review with SRE, Platform, SecOps next Tue (invitation in Slack).

References
- Confluence: RBAC V2 Overview (linked above)
- Jira: SEC-412 (schema tests), SEC-458 (postmortem template)
- GitHub: platform PR 789 (initial transform library)

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally pragmatic: the goal is minimal coupling with downstream SIEMs and deterministic hashes for forensic reconstruction. Expect smaller follow-ups to refine condition catalog and retention policies.
